title: Add rolling-baseline computation + regression detector (min sample size, deploy-window suppression)
author: Marcus Reed
description: Context: perf-canary is now generating stable request traffic for a curated workload matrix, but we still need a production-grade way to decide when the signal represents a real regression vs normal noise (warmup, cache effects, rollout churn, low sample slices). This PR adds baseline computation + regression detector logic for p95 latency and tokens/sec, with guardrails: (1) rolling median baseline (default 7d, configurable) computed per (model, region, gpu_sku, stream_mode, scheduler_mode) slice, (2) minimum sample size and minimum active time window before evaluating, (3) deploy-window suppression so we don’t page during known churn. What’s included: Baseline store + computation: a small in-process baseline cache backed by the existing metrics query client; baseline = rolling median of windowed aggregates (we query 5m buckets over lookback, then take median across buckets, so the baseline is robust to a few bad buckets). Detector: evaluates every eval_interval (default 60s). For each slice we compute current p95_latency_ms over current_window (default 30m) and current_tokens_per_sec over current_window; regression = (current - baseline) / baseline. Thresholds: config supports independent thresholds per metric, defaults: latency_p95_regression_pct=0.15 (15% worse) and tokens_per_sec_regression_pct=-0.12 (12% drop). Minimum sample size: require min_requests >= 200 per slice (configurable) and at least min_nonempty_buckets >= 4 in the current_window; otherwise we mark slice as INSUFFICIENT_DATA and do not alert. Deploy-window suppression: if deploy annotations indicate a runtime deploy in the slice’s region within suppress_after_deploy (default 25m), we still compute and emit detector state metrics but we suppress paging (state=SUPPRESSED_DEPLOY_WINDOW). The intent is to capture the signal for dashboards while avoiding paging storms during rollout churn; once outside the window, the detector will page if the regression persists. Alert payload: detector returns a structured alert payload (serialized as JSON string for now) including slice key, baseline values, current values, regression pct, sample sizes, suppression reason (if any), and links (dashboards + runbook placeholders). Implementation notes: We intentionally do not attempt to ‘learn around’ deploy windows by auto-updating baselines in that window; baseline is always computed from lookback excluding the most recent suppress_after_deploy minutes to reduce bias from fresh deploy instability. Tokens/sec: uses the runner’s existing timestamps; detector expects tokens/sec already computed as (total_output_tokens / (t_last_token - t_first_token)) aggregated in the metrics pipeline; we query that series as-is and apply the same baseline approach. Tests: added unit tests for baseline median math, slice gating (min sample size), suppression state transitions, and threshold comparisons including edge cases around baseline=0 and missing data. Follow-ups / out of scope: pinned known-good baseline mode (ADR path) is not implemented here; this PR is rolling median only. Also not wiring to real paging yet; this just emits detector_state + detector_event for the alert rule PR to consume.
commits: detector: add rolling median baseline computation over lookback window
detector: add min sample size + bucket gating for slice evaluation
detector: add deploy-window suppression based on deploy annotation series
config: add thresholds + window sizes + suppression settings
tests: baseline math, suppression, and insufficient-data cases

conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): The suppression window is important, but we should still surface that we would have paged (so we can tune thresholds). Do we have a metric/state for this? Marcus Reed (author): Yep—detector_state emits SUPPRESSED_DEPLOY_WINDOW with the computed regression_pct and sample sizes. The alert rule can optionally route suppressed events to a ticket channel later; for now it stays metrics-only. Nadia Rahman (review): Please confirm cardinality. You’re slicing by gpu_sku + scheduler_mode + stream_mode; that’s OK but we should avoid kernel_id or runtime_sha here. Marcus Reed (author): Agreed; detector only keys on the approved slice dimensions. runtime_build / sha is carried in the alert payload as best-effort enrichment from the deploy annotation series, not as a time-series label. Noah Patel (review): Baseline exclusion of the last suppression minutes makes sense. One concern: using 5m buckets and then median-of-buckets can hide short spikes. Do we want p95-of-30m as ‘current’ but median-of-5m buckets as ‘baseline’? Marcus Reed (author): That’s intentional: baseline is robust; current window is where we want sensitivity. If we see missed detections we can tighten bucket size or compute a baseline on p95-of-30m across lookback, but it tends to be noisier. Tomáš Novák (review): For insufficient data, please log at debug only; we don’t want noisy logs. Marcus Reed (author): Done in latest push (moved to debug, and emits a single metric with state=INSUFFICIENT_DATA). Sean Gallagher (follow-up): Can we make the suppression window configurable per region? Some regions deploy slower. Marcus Reed (author): Added optional per-region overrides in config (suppress_after_deploy_by_region). All reviewers approved after changes; merged via squash.
release_notes: Internal: perf-canary now computes rolling baselines and emits regression detector state/events with deploy-window suppression and sample-size gating.
